info.name: Cutera API
info.description:
Backend API collection for the Cutera admin + mobile clients.

## How to use

1. Import this collection into Postman.
2. Set `base_url` in **Collection Variables** (already defaults to `http://cutera-upgradation.test` for local dev).
3. Run **Auth → Login** once with a real admin email/password — the post-response script stores `access_token` + `refresh_token` on the collection.
4. Every other request inherits `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` from collection-level auth.
5. Access tokens expire in 15 minutes; run **Auth → Refresh** to rotate without re-entering credentials.

## Scope

- Auth (Passport password grant — v2)
- Application Users (CRUD, status, password change)
- Roles (CRUD + duplicate)
- Permissions (CRUD + parent groups)

More modules will be appended as they're requested.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Passport password-grant auth. Login stores access + refresh tokens on the collection so every other request authenticates automatically.

request.description:
Exchanges email + password for a Passport access/refresh pair. Rate-limited 5/min.

Response `data`: `{ access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, token_type, user }`.

exec: console.log('Stored access + refresh tokens on collection.');

request.description: Rotates the access + refresh token pair. Rate-limited 10/min.
Revokes the current access token and its refresh chain.

item.name: Users
item.description:
Application (staff/admin) users — CRUD, status toggle, password change.

`/api/users/datatable` returns a DataTables-style payload outside the standard envelope; on the SPA side call `api.post(path, body, { raw: true })`.

request.description: Paginated list with filters. Permission: `users_manage`.
Returns roles, locations, warehouses, user types needed to render the create form. Permission: `users_create`.
Password must be 8+ chars with upper, lower, digit, and special char. Permission: `users_create`.
User data + dropdowns for the edit form. Permission: `users_edit`.
Full user update. `email`, `phone`, `gender` required on PUT/PATCH. Permission: `users_edit`.
Soft-delete user. Permission: `users_destroy`.
Activate (status=1) or deactivate (status=0) a user. Permission: `users_active`.

variable.description: Encrypted user id — obtain from a previous endpoint, not the raw integer in production.

request.description: Returns the encrypted id used by the PATCH below. Permission: `users_change_password`.
⚠️ Current known auth gap: no re-auth / current_password check. Permission: `users_change_password`.

item.description:
Permission catalog management — CRUD plus a parent-group listing.

Note: this module's FormRequest returns `{ status:false, message, errors }` on 422 (no `success` key). The SPA's api client already handles that fallback.

item.name: Doctors
item.description: Doctor management — Doctors are a User subtype (`user_type_id = 5`) with a parallel `resources` row (`resource_type_id = 2`) for rotation/scheduling. The API lives under `/api/doctors/*`. Dashboard endpoints under `/api/doctor-dashboard/*` are for the doctor's own KPI view (gated by role, not a dedicated permission). Lookup endpoints (`/api/appointments/load-*`, `/api/get-doctors*`) are used by appointment and sales flows to pick a doctor.

request.description: Paginated doctor list. Filterable by name/email/phone/gender/role/status/date. Permission: `doctors_manage`.
Returns roles, locations, and service hierarchy needed to render the create form. Permission: `doctors_create`.
Creates a doctor (User with `user_type_id = 5` plus a Resources row). Password must be 8+ chars with upper, lower, digit, special char. Permission: `doctors_create`.
Returns the doctor + current location/service allocations + dropdown options for the edit form. Permission: `doctors_edit`.
Update doctor profile. `password` optional on update (omit to keep current). Permission: `doctors_edit`.
Soft-delete doctor. Also drives the datatable bulk-delete action when the SPA sends an id array. Permission: `doctors_destroy`.
Activate (`status=1`) or deactivate (`status=0`) a doctor. Two separate permissions — `doctors_active` for activation, `doctors_inactive` for deactivation.

variable.description: Encrypted doctor id used by the PATCH below.

request.description: Returns the encrypted id used when saving the new password. Permission: `doctors_change_password`.
Same no-re-auth caveat as the users endpoint. Permission: `doctors_change_password`.
Returns the location allocation list (allocated + available locations with `is_allocated` flag). Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Returns the service tree for a given doctor + location showing which services are allocated. Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Allocates services to a doctor for a location (persists to `doctor_has_locations` pivot). Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Unallocates services from a doctor for a location. Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Doctor-facing KPI metrics for the signed-in doctor. Gated by role (`Aesthetic Doctor` / `Lifestyle Consultant`) — not a dedicated permission.
Hero summary section for the doctor dashboard.
Today's appointments for the signed-in doctor.
Benchmark comparison data (⚠️ audit noted this method existence wasn't fully verified — may need backend confirmation).
Minimal `{id, name}` list for dropdown pickers (admin-config).
Doctors available for a given location/service/date — used by the appointment booking flow.
Doctors with `can_perform_consultation = 1` for a location.
Working hours / off days for a doctor on a given date.
Doctor picker for the sales/orders flow.
Generic doctor list (orders module).

item.name: User Types
item.description: User-type catalog — the `user_types` row that the `users.user_type_id` FK points at. Seeded values include Doctor (5), Patient (3), etc. Full CRUD + an active/inactive split using PATCH-by-id (NOT the POST `/status` pattern used by users and doctors). Dropdown + doctor-list helpers for pickers elsewhere in the app.

request.description: Paginated list. Permission: `user_types_manage`.
Dropdown / init data for the create form. Permission: `user_types_create`.
Permission: `user_types_create`.

item.name: HRM
item.description:
HRM module — employee management, leave mgmt, recruitment, notifications, self-service. Fiscal year is Jul–Jun (formatted `YYYY-YY`, e.g. `2025-26`). Leave durations are typed enums: Full=1.0, Half=0.5, Short=0.25.

**Current API surface is limited**: 4 datatables + 1 calendar feed + 3 notification endpoints. Employee CRUD, leave approve/reject/cancel, recruitment CRUD, and self-service flows are web-only today (`/hr/*`) and need API wrappers. See the backlog in `docs/audits/` (coming) for the build list.

request.description: Paginated employee list. Filters: `name`, `designation`, `status`, `location_id`. Permission: `hr_employees_view`.
Paginated leave applications. Filters: `status`, `leave_type`, `employee_name`, `date_from`, `date_to`. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Leave balance by employee for a fiscal year (`YYYY-YY` format — e.g. `2025-26`). Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Paginated candidates. `status` enum: `scheduled, in_review, shortlisted, on_hold, offer, hired, offer_declined, rejected, blacklisted`. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.
Approved/pending leave events for the vis-timeline calendar. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Signed-in user's recent HR notifications. Returns `{ notifications, unread_count }`. No permission gate — scoped to the current user.
Marks a single notification read. Ownership enforced in the controller.
Marks every notification for the current user as read.
Create employee (User + EmployeeDetail + location assignment in one transaction). Permission: `hr_employees_manage`. Returns `EmployeeResource` with 201.
Full employee profile with EmployeeDetail, documents, locations. Permission: `hr_employees_view`.
Update employee. `password` omitted keeps current. Permission: `hr_employees_manage`.
Soft-delete employee. Also revokes the user's Sanctum tokens so any live session dies. Permission: `hr_employees_manage`.
Activate (`status=1`) or deactivate (`status=0`). Response: `{ id, active }`. Permission: `hr_employees_manage`.

query.description: Admin-only filter. Non-admins are force-scoped to their own rows regardless.
Name search. Ignored for non-admin callers.

request.description: Paginated leave applications with employee + designation + leave type + reviewer eager-loaded. Callers without `hr_leave_view` are auto-scoped to their own applications — no 403. Response: `{ items, meta }` where each item is a `LeaveApplicationResource`.

body.raw:
{
  "user_id": 1,
  "leave_type_id": 1,
  "start_date": "2026-05-10",
  "end_date": "2026-05-12",
  "duration_type": "full",
  "custom_hours": null,
  "reason": "Applied on behalf — pre-planned vacation.",
  "auto_approve": false,
  "review_notes": null
}

request.description: HR creates a leave application on behalf of an employee. Reuses `LeaveService::apply` so overlap / shift-hour / balance checks stay centralised. Returns **409** on overlapping dates. `auto_approve=true` approves immediately and increments the balance. `duration_type`: `full` | `half` | `short` | `custom` (requires `custom_hours > 0`). Permission: `hr_leave_approve`.
Status counts for dashboards and badges: `{ pending, approved, rejected, cancelled, total }`. Filters apply to `start_date` within the window. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.

Month-scoped pending + approved applications for a calendar grid. Returns `{ month, year, items[] }` where each item is `{ id, user_id, user_name, leave_type, status, start_date, end_date, total_days }`. Mobile-friendly shape — see `calendar-data` for the legacy Vis-timeline shape. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.

Streams a CSV named `leave_applications_{timestamp}.csv` with columns: ID, Employee, Leave Type, Start Date, End Date, Duration, Total Days, Status, Reason, Applied On. Uses `chunkById(500)` so it stays safe on production-sized tables. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Application detail with reviewer, notes, leave type, and employee. Access: the applicant OR anyone with `hr_leave_view`.
`review_notes` optional. Permission: `hr_leave_approve`.
`review_notes` **required** (max 1000). Permission: `hr_leave_approve`.

Mirrors the web rule exactly: **pending** leave → applicant or `hr_leave_approve` can cancel; **approved** leave → only `hr_leave_approve` (not the applicant). Leave balance is refunded via the existing service.
Own profile (User + EmployeeDetail + locations + documents). No permission required — ownership via `Auth::id()`. Null-safe when no EmployeeDetail exists.

Allowlist-only: `phone`, `dob`, `gender`, `address`, emergency contact fields. Any other field (salary, department, manager, active) is silently dropped. If the user has no EmployeeDetail row, emergency-contact fields no-op (documented CUTERA-REVIEW).
Own balances (current fiscal year, `YYYY-YY`) + applications + shift_hours in one response.

`duration` enum: `full` (1.0) / `half` (0.5) / `short` (0.25) / `custom` (requires `custom_hours`). Overlap-checked and balance-warned via the existing `LeaveService`. Returns `LeaveApplicationResource` (201).
Edit own pending leave. 403 if not the applicant, 422 if status != pending.
Cancel own pending leave. Rejects approved leaves with 422 (that path is HR-only via `/leave-applications/{id}/cancel`).
Own employee documents with Google Drive upload status. Returns `EmployeeDocumentResource::collection`.

Account-scoped departments ordered by name. Callers with `hr_departments_manage` also see inactive entries; without it only active rows are returned. Each row includes `designations_count` and `employees_count`. Permission: `hr_departments_view`.
Single department with counts. 404 if the department belongs to a different account. Permission: `hr_departments_view`.

Create a department. `name` is required and must be unique per account (excluding soft-deleted rows). `active` defaults to `true`. Permission: `hr_departments_manage`. Returns `DepartmentResource` (201).
Update department name / active flag. Cross-account updates return 404. Permission: `hr_departments_manage`.
Soft-delete. Returns **409** if any employees are still assigned, or if designations exist under this department. Permission: `hr_departments_manage`.

query.description: Optional filter — designations belonging to a specific department.

request.description: Account-scoped designations with their department eager-loaded. Callers with `hr_designations_manage` also see inactive entries; otherwise only active rows are returned. Permission: `hr_designations_view`.
Single designation with its department. 404 if the designation belongs to a different account. Permission: `hr_designations_view`.

Create designation. `name` required and unique per account (excluding soft-deleted). `department_id` nullable but must belong to the caller's account. Permission: `hr_designations_manage`. Returns `DesignationResource` (201).
Update designation. Cross-account updates return 404. Permission: `hr_designations_manage`.
Soft-delete. Returns **409** if any employees are currently assigned to this designation. Permission: `hr_designations_manage`.

query.description: Optional. Defaults to the current fiscal year (e.g. `2025-26`).
Optional. Admin-only filter — non-admins always see just their own rows.

request.description: Paginated list of `leave_balances`, eager-loaded with `user` + `leave_type`. Callers without `hr_leave_manage` are force-scoped to their own `user_id`. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.

query.description: Optional. Defaults to the current fiscal year.

request.description: Employee × leave-type matrix for the given fiscal year. Returns `{ fiscal_year, leave_types[], rows[] }` where each row is `{ user_id, user_name, balances[{leave_type_id, leave_type_name, allocated, used, remaining}] }`. Permission: `hr_leave_manage`.
Returns the current fiscal year string plus its `start_date` and `end_date` (Jul 1 → Jun 30). Convenience endpoint for mobile filter chips. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.

query.description: Optional. Defaults to the current fiscal year.

request.description: All balances for a single employee in a given fiscal year. A user can always request their own balances; otherwise `hr_leave_manage` is required. Cross-account `user_id` returns 404.
Upsert a single employee's allocation for the given leave type + fiscal year. Returns `LeaveBalanceResource`. `allocated` is 0–365. `fiscal_year` must match `YYYY-YY`. Permission: `hr_leave_manage`.
Upsert the same allocation across many employees. `user_ids` must be 1–500 distinct ids, each belonging to the caller's account. Response includes `allocated_count`. Permission: `hr_leave_manage`.

query.description: Optional. Defaults to the current fiscal year.

request.description: Streams a CSV named `leave_balances_{fiscal_year}.csv` with one column per leave type × {Allocated, Used, Remaining}. Permission: `hr_leave_manage`.

Hard-delete a balance row. Returns **409** if `used > 0` (leave has already been drawn against it — HR must reduce `allocated` via `allocate` instead). Cross-account rows return 404. Permission: `hr_leave_manage`.
Active leave types. Callers with `hr_leave_manage` also see inactive entries. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Create leave type. Permission: `hr_leave_manage`. Returns `LeaveTypeResource` (201).
Permission: `hr_leave_manage`.
Soft-delete. Returns **409** if any `leave_applications` row references the type. Permission: `hr_leave_manage`.
